messages:
emma: Heads up — since the kernel-selector roll last night we're seeing a spike in OOMs on gpu-pool-a (started ~22:12 UTC). 30% of heavy requests fail with allocator OOM.
raj: Impact on SLOs?
morgan: Affected endpoint /v1/generate, error-rate ~12% and p95 latency +80ms. A few customer sessions dropped.
li: Looks like KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x, traces show frequent KV writebacks and workspace inflation.
emma: Relevant logs: ```OOM allocating workspace 2.3GB for model-xyz; peak_mem 61.4GB/64GB; attempting kv_eviction->fail```
emma: Immediate mitigation proposal (short checklist):
- enable kernel fallbacks (route to older kernel with conservative workspace sizing)
- enable temporary KV "swap-to-host" policy for cold segments (move >512KB entries to CPU RAM)
- drop batching to 1 for the top 5 latency-sensitive routes
- reduce concurrent requests via soft rate-limit for the pool to 60% of normal
raj: Commands to flip toggles: ```rbctl runtime set kernel_selector.enabled=false --pool=gpu-pool-a``` and ```rbctl runtime set alloc.headroom=0.14 --pool=gpu-pool-a```
li: For KV swap: ```rbctl kv-policy set --policy swap-to-host --threshold 524288 --pool=gpu-pool-a``` (this streams eviction metadata to host memory, not persistent)
morgan: I'll run them in order. Rolling kernel fallback now.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback started for kernel-selector on pool gpu-pool-a (canary=10%).
morgan: Canary looks good for 3 minutes, errors down to 4%. Proceeding to 50%.
emma: While we stabilize, throttle the heavy model route: ```ratectl set /v1/generate --pool=gpu-pool-a --qps 60```
li: Also start a live profiler snapshot and collect KV heatmap: ```gpu-prof snapshot --pool gpu-pool-a --out /tmp/snap-230555``` and ```kv-inspect heatmap --pool gpu-pool-a --out /tmp/kv-heat-230555```
emma: Quick runtime check to see if buffer reuse path is misallocating: paste output of `nvidia-smi` and `rbctl runtime metrics --pool gpu-pool-a | grep workspace` if you can.
raj: Observed an allocator regression in the kernel branch: reduced small-block coalescing so workspace fragmentation increased. Root cause looks like the new kernel's small-block allocator change.
li: Temporary config change to reduce fragmentation: ```rbctl runtime set alloc.small_block_coalesce=true --pool=gpu-pool-a```
morgan: Applied small_block_coalesce + headroom + kernel fallback + kv-swap. Monitoring. Errors down to 1.2%, p95 returning near baseline. :thumbsup:
emma: Ok, we stabilized the incident. Post-mortem action items:
- revert or patch kernel small-block allocator change and add unit/regression test for high-KV churn workloads
- add an automated circuit that flips kernel_selector->fallback when OOM% > 10% for 3m
- add an end-to-end perf test that simulates KV thrash + batch size 8 to catch workspace inflation regressions
- document KV swap policy caveats and set a 15m TTL for swap-evicted items to avoid long-term mem pressure on host
li: I'll own the regression test and the kernel patch.
raj: I'll add the automatic circuit and a dashboard alert for allocator fragmentation ratio.
morgan: I'll write the incident notes and schedule a retro. Anything else?
emma: Add a short runbook snippet for on-call: 1) enable kernel fallback 2) set alloc.headroom to 0.12-0.18 3) enable kv swap-to-host 4) throttle /v1/generate 5) reduce batching to 1. Keep it < 10 lines.
morgan: Will do. Closing the thread when retro created.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed, 0 failures in last 5m.
